title: Philly Cheesesteak Pizza
subtitle: Steak, peppers, provolone on dough
description: Steak, peppers, provolone on dough. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Sear steak and vegetables
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat. Sear steak in batches 2 minutes until browned but not overcooked — it finishes on the pie. Sauté peppers and onions in the same pan 10 minutes until soft and charred at edges. Season with salt, pepper, and Worcestershire.

steps.title: Combine steak, veg, and provolone
steps.instruction: Chop steak roughly and toss with peppers, onions, and torn provolone off heat so cheese starts to melt. This is your cheesesteak topping — keep warm.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 500°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 500°F at least 40 minutes. Stretch dough while the stone saturates.

steps.title: Aioli base and load topping
steps.instruction: Stretch rounds to 12–14 inches. Spread a thin layer of garlic aioli instead of tomato sauce. Layer mozzarella, then the hot steak-pepper-onion-provolone mix evenly.

steps.title: Bake until provolone browns
steps.instruction: Bake 11–14 minutes until cheese on top browns and the crust is crisp. Philly Cheesesteak Pizza should smell like the sandwich — if it smells only like bread, you skimped on the filling.

steps.title: Rest and cut
steps.instruction: Rest 3 minutes so molten cheese sets. Cut 8 slices per pie. Serve fast — cheesesteak topping stays best when the pie is hot off the stone.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Philly Cheesesteak Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Steak, peppers, provolone on dough. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
